$Comment: The binding row for the Yeti's fight in the Yeti Cave (EncounterManager/Christmas/
Christmas_Yeti_Encounter.json): what the server owes for it, which the script never describes. It
names the fight (NameKey, the Yeti's nameplate in npcs.lang, on the bar's Records tab, the Claims it
pays and every line that names it), binds the boss the library credits through the script's Boss
slot, and keeps the fight's records under the bucket christmas_yeti, a boss on Records' Bosses tab in
the Seasonal group, split by how many fought him (ByPartySize). The achievement Yeti Hunter counts
this fight by its id (ENCOUNTER_DEFEATED), so a wild Yeti in the snow never counts.
Participation decides each player's share of his daily Claim. A player's score is every point of
damage they deal the Yeti (DamageDealt, the server rule's 1.0), every point they deal the White
Wolves he calls (DamageToAdds), every point they take while in the fight (DamageTaken) and every
second they spend in it (Presence), each times its weight; their share is that score against the top
player's. The wolves weigh the most, so a player who keeps them off the rest of the party reads close
to the top. Raise DamageToAdds to pay that work more, raise Presence to flatten the shares, lower it
to reward damage more.
Feedback names its own notices under FeedbackMoments/SeasonsOfOrbis: a banner as he rises, a toast
with each player's share when he falls, and a toast after a wipe. His script tells the members of
each of its phases itself, so PhaseChanged is left to the library and never shows.
Scale holds only Companion, with Health and Damage on: where MMO Mob Scaling runs, it may scale the
Yeti's health and his own hits, read once as the fight begins; without Mob Scaling the switches do
nothing. Write no other Scale leaf: his fight scales his health with the party itself, one step per
player. No Loot either: his script pays his two Claims. Switch the row off with Enabled false, or
from mods/ziggfreedcommon/encounters.json under the key christmas_yeti_encounter.
